02 · Read like a writer

PERSUADE OR INFORM?

Both have a place in digital campaigns, but they use language differently. Classify each extract and use the evidence in the wording.

Requirement 2

One campaign, two jobs

Informative writing explains clearly using facts, examples and neutral language. Persuasive writing influences an audience using benefits, emotion, questions and a call to action.

1
“Our community pantry provides emergency food parcels to families across Bridgend. Each parcel contains enough essentials for three days.”
2
“No family should face an empty cupboard. Give £5 today and help turn worry into a warm meal.”
3
“Volunteers sort donations every Tuesday and Thursday. New volunteers receive a short induction before their first shift.”
4
“Could you spare one hour to change someone’s week? Join our volunteer team and be the reason a neighbour feels supported.”

KEY TERMS

Target audienceThe specific group a campaign is designed to reach.
PersuasiveWriting intended to influence what an audience thinks, feels or does.
InformativeWriting intended to explain accurately and clearly.
Call to actionA direct instruction telling the audience what to do next.
Visual hierarchyThe order in which design makes viewers notice information.
EngagementAudience interactions such as views, likes, shares, comments or clicks.
House styleA consistent system for colour, type, imagery, logo and layout.
CredibilityHow believable and trustworthy a message appears.
